title: Beyond the Positive Partial Transpose Squared Conjecture: The Qutrit Case
abstract: Entanglement swapping is a fundamental operation in quantum repeaters for establishing entanglement between distant parties. The positive partial transpose (PPT) squared conjecture asks whether two PPT entangled links can generate terminal entanglement through entanglement swapping, or equivalently, whether the composition of two PPT maps is always entanglement breaking. Motivated by this conjecture, we investigate the map-composition problem beyond the PPT setting. For qutrit completely positive (CP) maps, we prove that the composition of any CP map whose Choi matrix is $1$-undistillable with any CP map whose Choi matrix has Schmidt number at most two is entanglement breaking in either order. Moreover, we show that the cone of $1$-undistillable CP maps is exactly the largest qutrit cone of CP maps whose composition with every CP map whose Choi matrix has Schmidt number at most two is entanglement breaking in both orders. Finally, although map composition captures only the standard maximally entangled outcome in entanglement swapping, we prove that any $1$-undistillable two-qutrit state and any state of Schmidt number at most two cannot generate terminal entanglement under an arbitrary selective measurement on the intermediate systems.
summary: This paper extends the study of entanglement preservation beyond the standard PPT conjecture by analyzing map composition in the qutrit setting. It proves that combining 1-undistillable channels with low-Schmidt number channels results in entanglement breaking. This has direct implications for understanding limitations in quantum repeaters and entanglement swapping protocols.
main_problem: The paper investigates the EB-composability problem, which generalizes the PPT squared conjecture by analyzing whether the composition of two specific cones of quantum channels is always entanglement breaking.
main_result: For qutrit systems, the composition of maps from the 1-undistillable cone ($	ext{UND}_1$) and the Schmidt number $\le 2$ cone ($	ext{SP}_2$) is proven to be entanglement breaking in both orders.
method: The authors utilize the Choi–Jamiołkowski correspondence to translate state properties (like separability) into map properties, proving composition theorems for defined cones of completely positive maps.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on quantum channels acting on two-qutrit systems ($d=3$), specifically characterizing the behavior of $	ext{UND}_1$ and $	ext{SP}_2$ cones under map composition.
key_observables: Entanglement breaking (EB) property of composed maps, separability ($\in 	ext{SEP}$), and the Schmidt number of Choi matrices.
important_parameters: The dimension $d=3$ (qutrit case); the structure of the two cones $	ext{UND}_1$ and $	ext{SP}_2$.
main_assumptions: The results are proven specifically for the two-qutrit setting; map composition is compared against general selective measurements.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic for EB-composability, showing $(	ext{PPT}, 	ext{PPT})$ as a special case, and confirm inclusions like $	ext{PPT} \subseteq 	ext{UND}_1 \subseteq 	ext{SP}_2$ in the qutrit setting.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the EB-composability problem, proving composition theorems for $(	ext{UND}_1, 	ext{SP}_2)$ (Theorem 4), establishing the maximality of $	ext{UND}_1$ (Theorem 6), and finally translating these map results to a state-level entanglement swapping condition (Corollary 10).
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools for characterizing when quantum operations fail to preserve entanglement, which is crucial for designing robust quantum communication protocols.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: Schematic illustration of the EB-composability problem. Let CPEB be the set of ordered pairs (Φ, Ψ) of CP maps such that Φ ◦Ψ is entanglement breaking. (a) An ordered pair of cones (X, Y) is EB- composable precisely when CPEB contains the Cartesian product of the two cones X×Y; in the figure, we identify the ordered pair (X, Y) with this product. (b) In particular, if, in every dimension, an EB- composable pair (X, Y) satisfies PPT ⊆X and PPT ⊆Y, then the PPT squared conjecture holds.

FIG. 2: Schematic illustration of our EB-composability results in the qutrit setting. For qutrit CP maps, PPT ⊆UND1 ⊆SP2 [22], and both UND1 × SP2 and SP2 × UND1 are contained in CPEB (see Theorem 4). Consequently, (UND1 × SP2) ∩(SP2 × UND1) = UND1 × UND1 ⊆CPEB (Corollary 7). Since UND1 contains non-PPT maps, PPT × PPT ⊊UND1 × UND1. Moreover, when either component is fixed to be SP2, the largest compatible cone for the other component is exactly UND1 (see Theorem 6).

FIG. 3: Entanglement-swapping obstruction caused by a 1- undistillable link. When a two-qutrit link in UND1 is joined to a link in S2, in either order, every post-selected entanglement swapping outcome is separable. Consequently, the resulting state is separable, and subsequent entanglement swapping cannot generate end-to-end entanglement between A and Z.
